mainTopic: מוקצה of כלים: רבה's rereading of the early sources, the משנה of לצורך ושלא לצורך, and גזירה יום טוב אטו שבת
overview: This amud first finishes the list of sources (the poles, the thick-headed bolt, the mortar) that seemed to show some מוקצה rules came from before התרת כלים. רבה then argues that each source has its own reason. The rods and poles were not needed, the bolt is about carrying without an עירוב, and the mortar follows רבי נחמיה. Next comes a new משנה: the תנא קמא lets כלים be moved 'לצורך ושלא לצורך,' but רבי נחמיה allows only 'לצורך.' רבה defines these terms by the kind of item and the reason for moving it, using צורך גופו and צורך מקומו. רבא rejects that and gives his own definition, in which 'שלא לצורך' means even moving an item from sun to shade. The bowls question against רבה is answered by comparing dirty bowls to a chamber pot. אביי's challenges to רבא from the mortar, the pestle, and the firewood are answered with sun-to-shade, a decree on יום טוב because of שבת, and the rule that only a real כלי can be moved. Finally, two משניות clash over whether we decree יום טוב because of שבת. רב יוסף's answer is rejected, and רב פפא starts a new answer from בית שמאי and בית הלל that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the poles source: flaying the lamb using a friend's shoulder
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting the source about the poles (מקלות) used for flaying the קרבן פסח. On שבת they used a friend's shoulder instead of the poles.
steps.simpleTranslation: He places his hand on his friend's shoulder, and his friend's hand on his shoulder, and he hangs the lamb and flays its skin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote it started earlier: when ערב פסח falls on שבת, the poles are not used, so two people make a 'pole' out of their arms to hang and skin the קרבן פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of this source is that the poles were treated as מוקצה and could not be handled on שבת. The גמרא brings it as evidence that this ruling dates from before התרת כלים, when almost all כלים were forbidden to move.

keyTerms.meaning: Poles (used in the מקדש to hang the קרבן פסח for skinning)

phrases.english: his hand on the shoulder of his friend
phrases.notes: Continuation of the quoted source about the poles on שבת

phrases.english: and his friend's hand on his shoulder,
and he hangs [the lamb] and flays it.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָדוֹ עַל כֶּתֶף חֲבֵירוֹ וְיַד חֲבֵירוֹ עַל כְּתֵיפוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a source quotation begun on the previous amud
steps.raayaObject: That the poles were forbidden as מוקצה in the period before התרת כלים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about flaying the קרבן פסח when ערב פסח falls on שבת

steps.title: The source for the thick-headed bolt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה about a door bolt with a thick knob on its end. רבי יהושע and רבי טרפון argue about how it may be moved on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The thick-end case comes from what we learned in a משנה: a door bolt with a thick knob at its head. רבי יהושע says: one may drag it from this doorway and hang it in another doorway on שבת. רבי טרפון says: it is like all other כלים and may be moved in the courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second source, a bolt with a thick end (גלוסטרא). רבי יהושע allows only dragging it, not carrying it normally, while רבי טרפון lets it be moved like any כלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע's limit (drag it, don't lift it) looks like the bolt is being treated as מוקצה. So the גמרא suggests his view reflects the strict period before התרת כלים. רבי טרפון's lenient view fits the later period.

keyTerms.meaning: A thick knob or bulge on the end of a bolt
A door bolt (a bar used to lock a door)
Drags or slides it (without carrying it in the normal way)

phrases.english: The thick end, as we learned in a Mishnah:
a bolt that has a thick knob at its head,
Rabbi Yehoshua says:
one may drag it from this doorway
and hang it in another [doorway] on Shabbat.
Rabbi Tarfon says:
it is like all the [other] utensils
and may be moved in the courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the next source in the list
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהושע's restriction reflects the period before התרת כלים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of נגר שיש בראשו גלוסטרא

steps.title: The mortar source was already cited
steps.stepSummary: For the mortar (מדוכה), the גמרא points back to the source it already quoted earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: The mortar: that is what we already said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the last source, the mortar, and does not repeat it, since it was already quoted earlier in the סוגיא. This closes the list of sources.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier source said a mortar may be moved only if it has garlic in it, and otherwise not. That strictness was also taken as a sign of the period before התרת כלים.

keyTerms.meaning: Mortar (a bowl for crushing spices or garlic)

phrases.english: The mortar: that which we said [earlier].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final item in the list of sources
steps.raayaObject: That the mortar rule reflects the period before התרת כלים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The earlier-quoted source about the mortar

steps.title: רבה questions the whole proof
steps.stepSummary: רבה challenges the claim that these sources come from before התרת כלים. Maybe they were taught afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: How do you know? Perhaps I can tell you that these sources were really taught after the permission to move כלים was given.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה pushes back on the list of proofs. He suggests every source could come from the later, lenient period. This line sets up the next steps, where he explains each source one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed that strict rules about these items mean they belong to the early, strict period. רבה argues that each item could have its own special reason for being forbidden, even after general כלים were permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: The later permission to move כלים on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: רבה does not say these items are not מוקצה. He agrees they were forbidden. He only argues that the reason is something specific to each item, not the early strict period.

phrases.english: Rabba said: From where [do you know this]?
Perhaps, actually, I can say to you
[that] they were taught after the permission for utensils:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: מִמַּאי, דִּילְמָא לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לְךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn from all the sources
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: All four sources (קנים, מקלות, גלוסטרא, מדוכה)
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The sources can be explained by item-specific reasons even after התרת כלים

steps.title: Why the showbread rods were not moved
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains the rods (קנים) of the לחם הפנים. They prevent mold, and in the short time until שבת ends the bread will not get moldy, so moving them is pointless.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rods: what is their purpose? To keep the bread from getting moldy. In this short time it will not get moldy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה explains the first source: the rods placed between the loaves of the לחם הפנים were not handled on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rods exist only to let air in so the bread won't get moldy. Over the short time left on שבת the bread won't spoil, so there is no real need to handle them. With no need, moving them is forbidden even after התרת כלים.

keyTerms.meaning: Rods placed between the loaves of the לחם הפנים
A little bit (here: a short time)

phrases.english: The rods, what is the reason [for them]?
Because of [the bread] getting moldy;
in this short time it will not get moldy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבה's challenge to the first source
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rods are not moved because they serve no need on שבת, not because of the early strict period

steps.title: Why the poles were not used
steps.stepSummary: The poles were not needed, because the lamb can be flayed using the shoulder method.
steps.simpleTranslation: The poles: it is possible [to manage without them] using the method of רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה explains the second source: the poles were not used on שבת because there is another way to skin the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since people can hang the lamb on each other's shoulders (the method we saw in step 1), the poles are unnecessary. An unnecessary use does not justify moving them, even after התרת כלים.

keyTerms.meaning: It is possible (there is another way)
The תנא whose method uses hands on shoulders

phrases.english: The poles: it is possible [to manage] according to Rabbi Elazar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבה's challenge to the second source
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The poles are avoided only because an alternative method exists

steps.title: The bolt dispute is really about carrying in a courtyard
steps.stepSummary: Following רבי ינאי, the bolt case involves a courtyard without an עירוב. רבי יהושע and רבי טרפון disagree on whether the inside of a doorway counts as part of the house or part of the courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: The thick-end bolt follows רבי ינאי, who said: we are dealing with a courtyard that has no עירוב. רבי יהושע holds that the inside of the doorway counts as inside the house, so he would be moving a house utensil into the courtyard. רבי טרפון holds that the inside of the doorway counts as outside, so he is moving a courtyard utensil within the courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה explains the third source. The disagreement about the bolt is about עירוב rules, not מוקצה, so it has nothing to do with the period before התרת כלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without an עירוב, you may not carry a house utensil into a shared courtyard. רבי יהושע sees a bolt stored in the doorway as a house utensil, so it may only be dragged. רבי טרפון sees it as a courtyard utensil, so it may be moved freely in the courtyard.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא whose explanation רבה uses
A courtyard with no עירוב (joining of courtyards)
A utensil belonging to the houses

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read רבי יהושע as calling the bolt מוקצה. In רבה's reading his limit comes from carrying without an עירוב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This moves the bolt case out of the topic of מוקצה and into the topic of עירובי חצרות, so the proof about התרת כלים falls apart.

phrases.english: The thick end, according to Rabbi Yanai,
as Rabbi Yanai said:
we are dealing with a courtyard that has no eiruv,
Rabbi Yehoshua holds:
the inside of the doorway is considered like inside [the house]
and he would be moving a utensil of the houses in the courtyard.
And Rabbi Tarfon holds:
the inside of the doorway is considered like outside,
and he is moving a courtyard utensil within the courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבה's challenge to the third source
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The dispute concerns carrying in a courtyard without an עירוב, not מוקצה

steps.title: The mortar source follows רבי נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: The last proof, the mortar, is pushed aside. It does not show the law from before התרת כלים. It follows רבי נחמיה, who holds that a vessel may be moved only for its normal use.
steps.simpleTranslation: The mortar: that source follows רבי נחמיה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה, continuing his rejection from step 4, knocks down the final proof, the mortar. He says that source follows the opinion of רבי נחמיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier source said a mortar may be moved only if it has food in it. That sounded like an old, stricter law from before התרת כלים. רבה answers that it is simply רבי נחמיה's view: a vessel may be moved only for the use it was made for. So it says nothing about the time before התרת כלים.

keyTerms.meaning: A mortar, a bowl used for crushing spices or garlic
A תנא who is strict about moving vessels on שבת

steps.whatToRemember: All the proofs (the mortar, the rods, the poles, the bolt) have been pushed aside. None of them proves what the law was before התרת כלים.

phrases.english: The mortar: it is the view of Rabbi Nechemya.
phrases.notes: He holds a vessel may be moved only for its normal use, so the mortar may be moved only when it is being used for food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבה's run of rejections (rods, poles, bolt) and finishes with the mortar.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the mortar source as proof of the law before התרת כלים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The source can be explained as following one תנא's strict view, רבי נחמיה. It need not reflect an earlier time period.

steps.title: משנה: vessels moved with or without a purpose
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה: the תנא קמא says all vessels may be moved for a purpose and not for a purpose. רבי נחמיה says only for a purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: All vessels may be moved for a purpose and not for a purpose. רבי נחמיה says: they may be moved only for a purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives a disagreement about when vessels may be moved on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא is lenient: vessels may be moved 'לצורך' and 'שלא לצורך.' רבי נחמיה is strict: only 'לצורך.' The משנה does not explain what these words mean, so the גמרא will ask.

keyTerms.meaning: May be moved or carried (within a permitted area) on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: This is about מוקצה, moving objects by hand. It is not about carrying from one domain to another.

phrases.english: MISHNA: All vessels may be moved
for a purpose and not for a purpose.
Rabbi Nechemya says:
They may be moved only for a purpose.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ כׇּל הַכֵּלִים נִיטָּלִין לְצוֹרֶךְ וְשֶׁלֹּא לְצוֹרֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It ties in with the previous step, which mentioned רבי נחמיה's strict view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: all vessels may be moved for a purpose and not for a purpose. רבי נחמיה: only for a purpose.

steps.title: What do the two terms mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of 'for a purpose' and 'not for a purpose.'
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is 'for a purpose,' and what is 'not for a purpose'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the משנה's two terms mean. This sets up רבה's definitions in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taken literally, 'not for a purpose' would mean moving a thing for no reason at all. That sounds odd to allow. So the גמרא wants an exact definition of each term.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is 'for a purpose'
and what is 'not for a purpose'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the משנה's terms.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The definitions of לצורך and שלא לצורך.

steps.title: רבה defines the terms
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains the terms this way. 'For a purpose' means a permitted-use item moved to use it. 'Not for a purpose' means a permitted-use item moved for its spot. A forbidden-use item may be moved only to use it. רבי נחמיה applies that same limit even to permitted-use items.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: 'For a purpose' means moving an item made for permitted work, in order to use the item itself. 'Not for a purpose' means moving an item made for permitted work, because you need its spot. An item made for forbidden work may be moved to use it, but not because you need its spot. רבי נחמיה came to say: even an item made for permitted work may be moved to use it, but not because you need its spot.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the question. He sorts vessels into two kinds (permitted use and forbidden use) and two reasons for moving them (to use the item, or to clear its spot).
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבה, the תנא קמא allows a permitted-use item to be moved for either reason. A forbidden-use item (like a hammer) may be moved only to use it, not to clear its spot. רבי נחמיה is stricter: he treats even permitted-use items that way, so they may be moved only to use them.

keyTerms.meaning: An item whose main use is permitted on שבת (for example, a cup)
An item whose main use is forbidden on שבת (for example, a hammer)
Because you need the place where it is lying

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse the two pairs. One pair is about the kind of item (permitted use or forbidden use). The other pair is about why you are moving it (to use it, or to clear its spot).
steps.whyThisMatters: These categories (צורך גופו, צורך מקומו, מלאכתו לאיסור) are the basic building blocks of the laws of מוקצה for כלים.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
'For a purpose' means an item whose function is permitted,
moved in order to use the item itself.
'Not for a purpose' means an item whose function is permitted,
moved because its place is needed.
And an item whose function is forbidden:
to use the item itself, yes;
because its place is needed, no.
And Rabbi Nechemya came to say:
even an item whose function is permitted:
to use the item itself, yes;
because its place is needed, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה לְצוֹרֶךְ דָּבָר שֶׁמְּלַאכְתּוֹ לְהֶיתֵּר לְצוֹרֶךְ גּוּפוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: לצורך means a permitted-use item moved לצורך גופו. שלא לצורך means a permitted-use item moved לצורך מקומו. A forbidden-use item may be moved only לצורך גופו. רבי נחמיה limits even permitted-use items to לצורך גופו.

steps.title: רבא: needing the spot is a real purpose
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רבה. Moving an item because you need its spot is a real need, so how can it be called 'not for a purpose'?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Moving it because you need its spot, you call that 'not for a purpose'?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רבה's definition. He says the words 'not for a purpose' don't fit moving something to clear its spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If I move a cup because I need the table space, I clearly have a reason. So רבה's reading does not match the plain words of the משנה. This sets up a different definition, which the גמרא will give next.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
Moving it because its place is needed,
you call that 'not for a purpose'?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְצוֹרֶךְ מְקוֹמוֹ שֶׁלֹּא לְצוֹרֶךְ קָרֵית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's definition from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's definition of שלא לצורך as לצורך מקומו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Needing the item's spot is a real need, so calling it 'not for a purpose' does not fit the wording of the משנה.

steps.title: רבא gives his own explanation of the terms
steps.stepSummary: רבא redefines the terms. 'For a purpose' covers both using the item and needing its spot. 'Not for a purpose' means even moving it from sun to shade. רבי נחמיה limits permitted-use items to the same rules as forbidden-use items.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: 'For a purpose' means a permitted-use item moved either to use it or because its spot is needed. 'Not for a purpose' means even moving it from the sun to the shade. A forbidden-use item may be moved to use it or for its spot, yes. Moving it from sun to shade, no. רבי נחמיה came to say that even a permitted-use item may be moved to use it or for its spot, yes, but from sun to shade, no.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected רבה's explanation, רבא now offers his own reading of the משנה's two terms.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא moves 'needing its spot' into the 'for a purpose' category, which fixes his own complaint in step 12. 'Not for a purpose' now means protecting the item itself, such as moving it out of the sun. In רבא's reading, רבי נחמיה only forbids that sun-to-shade moving for permitted-use items. He still allows moving them for their spot.

keyTerms.meaning: An item whose normal use is permitted on שבת
An item whose normal use is forbidden on שבת
Moving the item in order to use it
Moving the item because you need the spot it is in
From the sun to the shade, to protect the item itself

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא: permitted-use items may be moved for any reason, even sun to shade. Forbidden-use items may be moved to use them or for their spot, but not sun to shade. רבי נחמיה treats permitted-use items like forbidden-use items.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבה and רבא. For רבה, 'for its spot' counted as 'not for a purpose.' For רבא, 'for its spot' counts as 'for a purpose.'

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
'For a purpose' means an object whose function is permitted,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לְצוֹרֶךְ גּוּפוֹ בֵּין לְצוֹרֶךְ מְקוֹמוֹ.
phrases.english: whether to use it or to use its place.
'Not for a purpose' means even from the sun to the shade.
And an object whose function is prohibited:
to use it or to use its place, yes;
from the sun to the shade, no.
And Rabbi Nechemya comes to say:
even an object whose function is permitted:
to use it or to use its place, yes;
from the sun to the shade, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts רבא's challenge in step 12, sets aside רבה's explanation, and gives a new answer to the question of step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבה: needing an item's spot counts as 'not for a purpose.'
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא: needing the spot counts as 'for a purpose.' 'Not for a purpose' means moving from sun to shade.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: לצורך means a permitted-use item moved לצורך גופו or לצורך מקומו. שלא לצורך means moving it even מחמה לצל. A forbidden-use item may be moved for גופו or מקומו but not מחמה לצל. רבי נחמיה applies that limit even to permitted-use items.

steps.title: How are empty bowls moved according to רבה's reading of רבי נחמיה?
steps.stepSummary: Three חכמים ask how, according to רבה's reading of רבי נחמיה, we are allowed to clear away bowls after a meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא, רב אחא בר הונא and רב הונא בר חנינא sat together and said: According to רבה's reading of רבי נחמיה, how are we allowed to move these bowls?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבה's explanation and asks a practical question that seems to be a problem for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבה, רבי נחמיה forbids moving even a permitted-use item just to free up its spot. After a meal, people clear away empty bowls only because they want the table space. So how is that allowed?

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב סָפְרָא וְרַב אַחָא בַּר הוּנָא
phrases.english: Rav Safra and Rav Acha bar Huna sat
and Rav Huna bar Chanina,
and they sat and said:
According to Rabbah, following Rabbi Nechemya,
these bowls, how do we move them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רבא's view and tests רבה's view against common practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How clearing used bowls fits רבה's strict reading of רבי נחמיה.

steps.title: רב ספרא: Dirty bowls are like a chamber pot
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא answers that dirty bowls may be removed just as a chamber pot may be removed, because they are disgusting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said to them: It is just like a chamber pot.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא answers the question with a comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even items that normally may not be moved may be taken away if they are disgusting, like a chamber pot. Used bowls with leftover food are disgusting in the same way. So removing them is allowed for that reason, not because their spot is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A chamber pot, which may be removed because it is disgusting

phrases.english: Rav Safra said to them:
It is just like a chamber pot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the bowls.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Dirty bowls are removed because they are disgusting, like a chamber pot.

steps.title: אביי asks רבה the same question
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רבה himself how bowls may be moved according to רבה's reading of רבי נחמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רבה: According to the Master's reading of רבי נחמיה, how do we move these bowls?
steps.whatsHappening: The same question is now put directly to רבה by his student אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same difficulty as before, but now רבה himself must respond. It shows the question was a real issue for רבה's approach.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the Master, a respectful way of saying 'according to you'

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rabbah:
According to the Master, following Rabbi Nechemya,
these bowls, how do we move them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the bowls question, now to רבה directly.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבה's own answer for how bowls are moved.

steps.title: רבה cites רב ספרא's chamber pot answer
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers with the explanation his colleague רב ספרא gave: it is like a chamber pot.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Our colleague רב ספרא explained it: It is just like a chamber pot.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה agrees with רב ספרא's answer and quotes it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה confirms that his view holds up. Dirty bowls are moved because they are disgusting, not because their spot is needed.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה, clearing dirty dishes is allowed because they are disgusting, like a chamber pot.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Rav Safra, our colleague, explained it:
It is just like a chamber pot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי with רב ספרא's explanation.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Bowls are moved because they are disgusting, like a chamber pot.

steps.title: אביי challenges רבא from the mortar
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a teaching that an empty mortar may not be moved. This seems to contradict רבא, who allows moving vessels to use them or for their spot.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged him: A mortar, if it has garlic in it, may be moved. If not, it may not be moved.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's explanation with a teaching about a mortar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבא, even a forbidden-use item may be moved to use it or for its spot. So why would an empty mortar be completely forbidden to move? The teaching seems stricter than רבא allows.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him from a teaching

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: מְדוֹכָה, אִם יֵשׁ בָּהּ שׁוּם — מְטַלְטְלִין אוֹתָהּ,
phrases.english: A mortar: if it has garlic in it, one may move it;
and if not, one may not move it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the bowls discussion and attacks רבא's view from step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that vessels may be moved to use them or for their spot.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A teaching forbids moving an empty mortar at all, which seems stricter than רבא allows.

steps.title: The mortar case is moving it from sun to shade
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the forbidden case is moving the empty mortar from sun to shade, which רבא also forbids.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are we dealing with here? Moving it from the sun to the shade.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends himself by narrowing the case in the teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching does not forbid moving the mortar to use it or for its spot. It only forbids moving it to protect it from the sun. That matches רבא's own rule.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? Used to narrow a source to a specific case

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
From the sun to the shade.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's mortar challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The teaching forbids moving an empty mortar for any reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: It only forbids moving it from sun to shade.

steps.title: אביי challenges רבא from the pestle used for cutting meat
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes another teaching about a pestle (עלי). בית שמאי and בית הלל agree that once meat was cut on it on יום טוב, it is forbidden to move it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him again: They agree that if one chopped meat on it, it is forbidden to move it!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a second source against רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here בית שמאי and בית הלל agree that the pestle (עלי) may not be moved after meat was cut on it on יום טוב. According to רבא, even a forbidden-use כלי should at least be movable for its use or for its spot. So this teaching again seems stricter than רבא.

phrases.english: He raised an objection:
And they agree that if one chopped meat on it
that it is forbidden to move it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ וְשָׁוִין שֶׁאִם קִצֵּב עָלָיו בָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to רבא, after the mortar was answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's permissive rule for moving vessels.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An agreed teaching forbids moving the pestle (עלי) once meat was cut on it, which seems to contradict רבא.

steps.title: Here too it means moving from sun to shade
steps.stepSummary: The same answer: the forbidden moving is from sun to shade.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it means from the sun to the shade.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the second challenge the same way as the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pestle may still be moved to use it or for its spot. The teaching only forbids moving it to protect it from the sun. So רבא's explanation stands.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's view survives both challenges. Sources that forbid moving a vessel are explained as talking about moving it from sun to shade.

phrases.english: Here too, from the sun to the shade.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the pestle challenge using the same idea as step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The pestle may not be moved for any reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only moving it from sun to shade is forbidden.

steps.title: A משנה forbids propping a pot with a piece of wood
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבא from a משנה that forbids propping a pot or a door with a piece of wood, even though on יום טוב wood is an item with a permitted use.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there is what we learned in a משנה: one may not prop up a pot with a piece of wood, and likewise a door. But on יום טוב a piece of wood is an item whose main use is permitted, since it may be burned. So it seems that even an item whose main use is permitted is forbidden to move, whether for using it or for using its spot!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings another משנה to challenge רבא's lenient view on moving items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא holds that a דבר שמלאכתו להיתר (an item with a permitted use) may be moved to use it or to free up its spot. On יום טוב, wood may be burned for cooking, so it should fit that category. Yet the משנה forbids using it to prop a pot, which seems to contradict רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: an item whose main use is permitted

phrases.english: And there is what we learned in a Mishnah:
One may not prop up the pot with a piece of wood
and likewise a door.
phrases.notes: One may also not prop a door with wood.

phrases.english: But a piece of wood, on Yom Tov,
is an item whose main use is permitted,
phrases.notes: It may be burned for cooking on Yom Tov.

phrases.english: so apparently an item whose main use is permitted,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לְצוֹרֶךְ גּוּפוֹ בֵּין לְצוֹרֶךְ מְקוֹמוֹ
phrases.english: whether to use the item itself or to use its spot,
is forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a third challenge by אביי in the same series, following the mortar and the chopping block.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that a דבר שמלאכתו להיתר may be moved for its use or its spot.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Wood is usable on יום טוב, yet the משנה forbids using it as a prop. That suggests usable items may not be moved even for their use.

steps.title: The wood is forbidden as a decree because of שבת
steps.stepSummary: The prohibition on יום טוב is only a decree, because on שבת the wood has no permitted use.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, what is the reason? Since on שבת the wood is an item whose main use is forbidden, חכמים decreed that it is also forbidden on יום טוב, because of שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי: the משנה's prohibition on יום טוב is a decree borrowed from שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On its own terms, wood on יום טוב would be permitted. Wood cannot be burned on שבת, though, so there it counts as forbidden. חכמים did not want people to confuse the two days, so they forbade it on יום טוב as well. רבא's rule therefore still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: an item whose main use is forbidden
because of / out of concern for

phrases.english: There, what is the reason?
Since on Shabbat
it is an item whose main use is forbidden,
there is a decree on Yom Tov because of Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the reason: the prohibition is a decree, not the basic law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה shows that usable items may not be moved at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wood is forbidden on יום טוב only because of a decree based on שבת.

steps.title: But even on שבת it should be allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא anticipates a challenge: on שבת itself, even items with a forbidden use may be moved for their use or their spot, so why is the wood forbidden?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: let it be permitted even on שבת itself, since even an item whose main use is forbidden may be moved to use it or to use its spot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible objection to its own answer and sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 23 assumed the wood is forbidden on שבת. But according to רבא, even a דבר שמלאכתו לאיסור may be moved לצורך גופו ומקומו. If so, there is nothing on שבת to base a decree on.

phrases.english: And if you will say:
let it be permitted on Shabbat itself,
since an item whose main use is forbidden,
to use it itself or to use its spot, is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the basis of the answer given in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 23 that wood is forbidden on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On שבת, even forbidden-use items may be moved for their use or spot, so wood should be allowed there too.

steps.title: The leniency applies only to real vessels
steps.stepSummary: Moving a forbidden-use item for its use or its spot is allowed only for a כלי, and a piece of wood is not a כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: That rule applies only where the item has the status of a vessel. Where it does not have the status of a vessel, it does not apply.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection: the lenient rule is limited to כלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A forbidden-use vessel, such as a hammer, may be moved for its use or its spot because it is still a כלי. A plain piece of wood is not a vessel at all, so on שבת it is completely מוקצה. That gives a real basis for the decree on יום טוב.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two categories. A דבר שמלאכתו לאיסור that is a real כלי can be moved for its use or spot. Wood is not a כלי at all, so on שבת it cannot be moved for any reason.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a key line in the laws of מוקצה: the leniencies for moving items depend on the item being a כלי.

phrases.english: This applies only
where the status of a vessel applies to it;
where the status of a vessel does not apply to it,
no.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא תּוֹרַת כְּלִי עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the lenient rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any forbidden-use item may be moved for its use or spot.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a real כלי gets that leniency, so wood is fully forbidden on שבת.

steps.title: Do we really decree on יום טוב because of שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the idea of a decree based on שבת, citing a משנה that permits dropping fruit through a skylight on יום טוב but not on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really make such decrees? But we learned in a משנה: one may lower fruit through a skylight on יום טוב, but not on שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea used in step 23, that חכמים forbid things on יום טוב because of שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this משנה, something forbidden on שבת is permitted on יום טוב, and no decree was made. This suggests חכמים do not automatically forbid on יום טוב whatever is forbidden on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: a skylight / opening in the roof

phrases.english: And do we really decree?
But we learned in a Mishnah:

phrases.aramaic: מַשִּׁילִין פֵּירוֹת דֶּרֶךְ אֲרוּבָּה בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: One may drop fruit through a skylight on Yom Tov,
but not on Shabbat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the principle of a decree on יום טוב because of שבת, which was used in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle גזירה יום טוב אטו שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה permits on יום טוב what is forbidden on שבת, showing no such decree was made.

steps.title: A second משנה suggests we do decree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings an opposing משנה: the only difference between יום טוב and שבת is food preparation, which suggests that everything else, including decrees, is the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do we really not make such decrees? But we learned in a משנה: the only difference between יום טוב and שבת is the preparation of food!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the other way and creates a clash between two משניות. It is setting up a resolution that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה implies that יום טוב and שבת share the same rules, including rabbinic decrees, except for food preparation. That conflicts with the skylight משנה. The גמרא now has to reconcile the two sources.

keyTerms.meaning: and do we really not decree?

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not settle the question. It sets two משניות against each other. רב יוסף answers in the next step (step 28).

phrases.english: And do we really not decree?
But we learned in a Mishnah:
There is no difference between Yom Tov and Shabbat
except food preparation alone!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 26 with a contradicting משנה, creating a clash between two sources.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication from step 26 that no decrees are made on יום טוב because of שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the only difference is food preparation, then all other שבת restrictions, including decrees, apply on יום טוב.

steps.title: רב יוסף: The Two משניות Follow Two Different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף resolves the contradiction by assigning each משנה to a different תנא. The stricter משנה follows רבי אליעזר and the more lenient one follows רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: This is not difficult. This משנה follows רבי אליעזר, and that משנה follows רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the contradiction from the last step. He says the two משניות are not by the same author, so they are allowed to disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of forcing both משניות into one view, רב יוסף says they reflect a real argument between תנאים. The strict משנה, where everything except food preparation is the same as שבת, matches רבי אליעזר. The lenient משנה, which allows dropping fruit on יום טוב, matches רבי יהושע. His proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This opens an answer to a contradiction.
This one... that one... Used to assign each source to a different case or opinion.
An אמורא who offers the first answer here.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: it is not difficult.
This one follows Rabbi Eliezer,
phrases.notes: The stricter משנה (יום טוב is like שבת except for food preparation).

phrases.english: that one follows Rabbi Yehoshua.
phrases.notes: The lenient משנה (fruit may be dropped through a skylight on יום טוב).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction between the two משניות raised in steps 26-27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing each source to a different תנא (מחלוקת תנאים)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות seemed to follow one view, so they contradicted each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The strict משנה follows רבי אליעזר and the lenient one follows רבי יהושע.

steps.title: The ברייתא of the Mother and Offspring in the Pit
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף brings a ברייתא as his source. A mother animal and its offspring fell into a pit on יום טוב, and you may not slaughter both on the same day. רבי אליעזר lets you lift out only the first and only feed the second. רבי יהושע lets you use a trick to lift out both.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: If 'it and its offspring' fell into a pit, רבי אליעזר says: one raises the first in order to slaughter it, and slaughters it. For the second, one provides food for it where it is so it will not die. רבי יהושע says: one raises the first in order to slaughter it and then does not slaughter it. Then he uses a trick and raises the second. Whichever one he wants, he slaughters.
steps.whatsHappening: This is רב יוסף's proof that רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע disagree about how lenient to be on יום טוב. רבי אליעזר is strict and רבי יהושע allows a trick to prevent a loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You may lift an animal out of a pit on יום טוב only if you plan to slaughter it for food. Since you cannot slaughter both mother and child that day, the second animal has no food purpose. רבי אליעזר therefore says to leave it and feed it. רבי יהושע allows a trick (הערמה) to save the owner's money. He says 'I changed my mind' and lifts the second one too. This suggests רבי יהושע relaxes rules on יום טוב to prevent loss, just as the lenient משנה does.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition against slaughtering a mother animal and its offspring on the same day (ויקרא כב:כח).
Sustenance, meaning feeding the animal where it is.
Uses a trick or legal maneuver (הַעֲרָמָה).
It was taught in a ברייתא.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ברייתא is about animal welfare or the איסור of אותו ואת בנו for its own sake. The גמרא only uses it to show how strict or lenient each תנא is on יום טוב when money is at stake.

phrases.english: As it was taught: 'it and its offspring'
that fell into a pit (on Yom Tov),
Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲלֶה אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹן עַל מְנָת לְשׁוֹחְטוֹ, וְשׁוֹחֲטוֹ.
phrases.english: one raises the first in order to slaughter it, and slaughters it.
And the second: one provides food for it in its place
phrases.notes: It may not be lifted out, since it cannot be slaughtered today.

phrases.english: so that it will not die.
Rabbi Yehoshua says:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲלֶה אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹן עַל מְנָת לְשׁוֹחְטוֹ, וְאֵינוֹ שׁוֹחֲטוֹ,
phrases.english: one raises the first in order to slaughter it, and does not slaughter it,
and uses a trick and raises the second,
phrases.notes: He claims he now prefers to slaughter the second one.

phrases.aramaic: רָצָה — זֶה שׁוֹחֵט, רָצָה — זֶה שׁוֹחֵט.
phrases.english: if he wants, he slaughters this one; if he wants, he slaughters that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind רב יוסף's assignment of the משניות to רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע disagree about relaxing יום טוב restrictions to prevent financial loss.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of אותו ואת בנו that fell into a pit.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר May Be Strict Only Because Feeding Is Possible
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב יוסף's proof. רבי אליעזר may forbid lifting the second animal only because it can be fed in the pit. Where there is no alternative, he might be lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you know this? Perhaps רבי אליעזר only said this there because feeding it is possible. But where feeding is not possible, he would not say so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב יוסף. It shows that רבי אליעזר's strictness in the pit case may not prove he is strict in general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the pit case the owner loses nothing, because feeding the animal keeps it alive. So רבי אליעזר's ruling may only mean 'don't be lenient when there is an easy alternative.' With fruit on a roof there is no such alternative. רבי אליעזר might then agree you may drop the fruit, so he need not be the author of the strict משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know this? This challenges a proof.
He only said this... in this specific case. Used to limit an opinion to its own case.

phrases.english: From where (do you know this)?

phrases.aramaic: דִּילְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָתָם
phrases.english: Perhaps Rabbi Eliezer only said (his ruling) there
because it is possible (to save it) by feeding,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר בְּפַרְנָסָה לָא.
phrases.english: but where it is not possible by feeding, he would not (forbid it).

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? דִּילְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inference רב יוסף drew from רבי אליעזר's view in the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from רבי אליעזר's side of the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His strictness may depend on an available alternative (feeding), which does not exist in the fruit case.

steps.title: רבי יהושע May Be Lenient Only Because a Trick Is Available
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, רבי יהושע may allow lifting the second animal only because a trick makes it look permitted. Where no trick is possible, he might forbid it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively, רבי יהושע only said this there because using a trick is possible. But where using a trick is not possible, he would not permit it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב יוסף's proof from the other side, showing that רבי יהושע's leniency may also be limited to the pit case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע did not simply permit lifting an animal with no food purpose. He allowed it only through a trick, where the owner claims he might slaughter this one. Dropping fruit through a skylight has no such trick. So רבי יהושע might forbid it, and he need not be the author of the lenient משנה. Since neither side of the ברייתא clearly matches the משניות, רב יוסף's answer falls.

keyTerms.meaning: Alternatively. This introduces a second, separate point.

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף's answer falls because each תנא's ruling in the pit case may depend on its special details: feeding for רבי אליעזר, the trick for רבי יהושע. Neither ruling clearly carries over to dropping fruit.

phrases.english: Alternatively,

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הָתָם
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua only said (his ruling) there
because it is possible through a trick,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר בְּהַעֲרָמָה — לָא!
phrases.english: but where it is not possible through a trick, he would not (permit it)!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי, עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, parallel rejection of רב יוסף's proof, this time from רבי יהושע's side.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from רבי יהושע's side of the ברייתא, which completes the rejection of רב יוסף's answer.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His leniency may depend on the availability of הערמה, which is absent in the fruit case.

steps.title: רב פפא: The משניות Follow בית שמאי and בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives a new answer: one משנה follows בית שמאי and the other follows בית הלל. He begins quoting his source, a משנה, which continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: This is not difficult. This one follows בית שמאי, and that one follows בית הלל. As we learned in a משנה: בית שמאי say:
steps.whatsHappening: After רב יוסף's answer was rejected, רב פפא offers a different pair of disputants. This step also sets up the next move: the quote of his source משנה begins here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא signals that the earlier answer has been dropped. רב פפא keeps the same strategy of assigning each משנה to a different side of a dispute. He uses the famous dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל instead. Which משנה goes with whom will become clear from the source that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the previous answer is set aside.
An אמורא who gives the new answer.
The two classic schools of תנאים.
As we learned in a משנה.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לָא קַשְׁיָא,
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said: it is not difficult.

phrases.aramaic: הָא — בֵּית שַׁמַּאי, הָא — בֵּית הִלֵּל.
phrases.english: This one follows Beit Shammai; that one follows Beit Hillel.
As we learned in a mishna: Beit Shammai say:
phrases.notes: The quote continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב יוסף's rejected answer with a new attribution of the two משניות.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing each source to a different side of a dispute (בית שמאי and בית הלל)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יוסף's pairing of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע was shown not to fit.
steps.terutzMaskana: The two משניות reflect the dispute of בית שמאי and בית הלל, with the source to follow.
